item.title: [Featured Article] Ashton-under-Lyne
item.description: Ashton-under-Lyne, also known as Ashton, is a market town in Tameside, Greater Manchester, United Kingdom. The population was 48,604 at the 2021 census. Historically a part of Lancashire, it is on the north bank of the River Tame, in the foothills of the Pennines, six miles east of Manchester.

item.title: [In the News] A new species of tiger cat is formally identified.
item.description: The tilcayo is a species of small wildcat in the genus Leopardus native to Bolivia. Identified through a genetic study of tiger cats published in September 2026, the tilcayo is the first extant cat species formally described since 1923. The tilcayo was already known to local communities under that name. Its visual appearance is extremely similar to that of other tiger cat species, with its status as a genetically distinct population not being documented by zoologists until the 2026 study.

item.title: [In the News] Former leader of Kosovo Hashim Thaçi is sentenced to twenty-five years in prison for war crimes during his leadership of the Kosovo Liberation Army.
item.description: Hashim Thaçi is a Kosovan politician and convicted war criminal. He was the first prime minister of Kosovo (2008–2014) and the foreign minister and deputy prime minister (2014–2016) in the cabinet led by Isa Mustafa. He served as president of Kosovo from 2016 until his resignation in 2020.

item.title: [In the News] In Turkey, hundreds of people are arrested in a crackdown on LGBTQ expression and subsequent protests.
item.description: In the early morning of 13 September 2026, prosecutors and courts started a crackdown on LGBTQ+ advocacy groups in Turkey and HIV advocacy groups, which then evolved into attacks on journalists, politicians, and protesters. The government justification for the crackdowns refers to a controversial policy called "My Family is Safe".

item.title: [In the News] A ferry sinks in the Java Sea, resulting in at least nine deaths and more than a hundred others missing.
item.description: On 13 September 2026, the Indonesian-flagged ferry Virgo Transport 8 capsized and sank in the Java Sea. The ferry was travelling from Surabaya, East Java to Banjarmasin, South Kalimantan, carrying 243 people and 89 vehicles. The sinking has resulted in at least 9 deaths, while 108 people have been rescued and 126 people remain missing.

item.title: [Most Read #1] Lizzie Borden
item.description: Daily Views: 896,572 — Lizzie Andrew Borden was an American woman who was tried and acquitted of the August 4, 1892 axe murders of her father and stepmother in Fall River, Massachusetts. No other individuals were charged with the murders.

item.title: [Most Read #2] Duncan Sheik
item.description: Daily Views: 319,023 — Duncan Scott Sheik was an American singer-songwriter, composer, and actor. Sheik is known for his 1996 debut single "Barely Breathing", which earned him a Grammy Award nomination for Best Male Pop Vocal Performance. He composed music for motion pictures and Broadway musicals, winning the 2007 Tony Awards for Best Original Score and Best Orchestrations for his work on the musical Spring Awakening.

item.title: [Most Read #3] Resident Evil (2026 film)
item.description: Daily Views: 289,025 — Resident Evil is a 2026 horror film directed by Zach Cregger and written by Cregger and Shay Hatten, based on the Resident Evil video game franchise by Capcom. It is the second reboot and overall eighth film in the Resident Evil film series. It follows Bryan, a young medical courier who must fight through an outbreak of infected monsters in Raccoon City. Zach Cherry, Kali Reis, and Paul Walter Hauser feature in supporting roles.

item.title: [Most Read #4] Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story
item.description: Daily Views: 232,203 — Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story is the fourth season of the American biographical crime drama anthology television series Monster, created by Ian Brennan for Netflix. The season centers on murder suspect Lizzie Borden who was tried and acquitted of the 1892 axe murders of her father and stepmother in Fall River, Massachusetts. It also stars Vicky Krieps, Charlie Hunnam, Rebecca Hall, Jessica Barden, Joey Pollari, Billie Lourd and Sarah Paulson. It is the first installment of the anthology to focus on an alleged female perpetrator.

item.title: [Most Read #5] Tilcayo
item.description: Daily Views: 156,503 — The tilcayo is a species of small wildcat in the genus Leopardus native to Bolivia. Identified through a 2026 genetic study of tiger cats, the tilcayo is the first cat species formally described since 1923. The tilcayo was already known to local communities but its visual appearance is extremely similar to other tiger cat species and the tilcayo had not been understood to actually be genetically distinct until this study revealed so.

item.title: [Most Read #6] Big Brother 28 (American season)
item.description: Daily Views: 153,156 — Big Brother 28 is the twenty-eighth season of the American reality television program Big Brother. The program is an adaptation of the franchise created in 1999 by John de Mol Jr.. The season features a time travel theme. It premiered on CBS on July 9, 2026, and is scheduled to conclude on October 1, 2026.

item.description: Daily Views: 126,661 — Patricia Stephanie Cole was an English stage, television, radio, and film actress, known for high-profile roles in shows such as Tenko (1981–1985), Open All Hours (1982–1985), A Bit of a Do (1989), Waiting for God (1990–1994), Keeping Mum (1997–1998), Doc Martin (2004–2009), Ed Reardon's Week (2005–2021), Cabin Pressure (2008–2014), Coronation Street (2011–2013), Still Open All Hours (2013–2019), and Man Down (2014–2017).

item.title: [Most Read #9] Ella Beatty
item.description: Daily Views: 117,999 — Ella Beatty is an American actress and the daughter of Annette Bening and Warren Beatty.

item.title: [Most Read #10] Killing of the Clancy children
item.description: Daily Views: 113,473 — On January 24, 2023, Lindsay Clancy fatally strangled her three children—five-year-old Cora, three-year-old Dawson, and eight-month-old Callan—at the family's home in Duxbury, Massachusetts, United States. She then attempted suicide by cutting her wrists and neck and jumping from a second-story window, sustaining injuries that left her paralyzed from the waist down. Lindsay later said she heard an auditory hallucination commanding her to commit the acts and felt unable to resist.
